neighbours.label: The comeback in an English two-way judgement: when one person has labelled another and the second person labels the first back (I think her a maverick, and she thinks me a stickler), the word opening the second label ('a', 'as').
neighbours.short: the comeback in a mutual labelling ('...and she thinks me a')
neighbours.notes: Sparse pole (0.159% > 0.1 max). Probing: lone labels ('Anna thinks him a bore') ~0.01; mirrored ('Tom thinks Anna lazy, and she thinks him a bore') 0.48; object as target ('the movie a bore') 0.03. globalMOO inverse found no leak; German mirrored judgement silent-ish (0.15), so scoped to English. fire: I think her a maverick, and she thinks me a stickler.
He considers his brother a dreamer, while his brother considers him a bore.
The coach sees the striker as lazy, and the striker sees the coach as a tyrant.
My aunt calls my uncle a spendthrift, and he calls her a miser in return.
She regarded him as reckless; he, in turn, regarded her as timid.
The critic dismissed the novelist as a hack, and the novelist dismissed the critic as a failed writer.
Tom finds Jerry a nuisance, and Jerry finds Tom a bully.
The old farmer thought the city girl a snob, and she thought him a grump.
quiet: I think her a maverick, and she rarely thinks about me at all.
He considers his brother a dreamer, and his brother lives in a small flat by the sea.
The coach sees the striker as lazy, and the striker trains alone every morning.
My aunt calls my uncle a spendthrift, and he buys a new hat every week.
She regarded him as reckless; he, in turn, ignored her completely.
The critic dismissed the novelist as a hack, and the novelist wrote a new book anyway.
Tom finds Jerry a nuisance, and Jerry hides in a hole in the wall.
The old farmer thought the city girl a snob, and she left the village after a week.
